method: every identifier is discovered from source and reported as integer code points; no name is compared as rendered text

characterisation.finding: NO Unicode homoglyph collision exists. The two runtime-home identifiers are pure ASCII, are unchanged by NFKC, differ at all eight positions of the shorter name, and differ visibly in length. The earlier description was wrong. What is real is a DISPLAY-LEVEL LOSS: evidence that records only rendered text cannot tell a reader which identifier a line refers to, and that is what caused a caller's redirection to be inert.

resolver.note: the resolver sets EVERY accepted name, so a spawned child cannot boot against a different home than its parent

verdict.assessment: the pair is not a Unicode collision; it is two distinct ASCII identifiers whose difference a text-only evidence artefact cannot express. The shared resolver accepts and sets both, which makes a caller's assignment effective either way.
